extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges (and State officials performing plan management), HHS program staff, and stakeholders commenting on SEIPM/Exchange oversight
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory proposal establishing requirements, data submissions, sampling, definitions, timelines, and oversight processes for a State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) program to measure APTC improper payments administered by State Exchanges and to report aggregated improper payment estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency for Effective Provider Access Review Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on what level of transparency is necessary and appropriate to safeguard public trust in Effective Provider Access Review Programs; which elements of process and which outputs of such programs should be subject to public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No specific form of new disclosure is being mandated at this time; the agency requests public feedback on elements of process and outputs that might warrant disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Essential Community Provider (ECP) Review Program eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning PY 2027, FFE States (including States performing plan management) may elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews of an issuer's plans applying for QHP certification through an FFE provided the State demonstrates sufficient authority and technical capacity to satisfy HHS criteria to be considered to have an Effective ECP Review Program (proposed §155.1051).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must satisfy applicable criteria established by HHS demonstrating authority and technical capacity; further details discussed elsewhere in the rule (III.E.11.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow SEIPM to satisfy certain annual independent external programmatic audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment to §155.1200 would permit State Exchanges to satisfy certain requirements of the independent external programmatic audit (outlined in §155.1200(d)) by completing the proposed State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) process (proposed §155.1200(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relief would be limited to compliance with 45 CFR part 155, subparts D and E as specified in guidance; HHS would continue to require audits for other subparts. Purpose is to reduce duplication and burden while maintaining oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish SEIPM purpose and scope (§155.1600)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEIPM is an HHS initiative through which HHS measures improper payments of APTC administered by State Exchanges, uses SEIPM results to produce an estimate of improper payments aggregated across State Exchanges, and would require annual submission of information from State Exchanges unless specified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS would publish aggregated improper payment estimates in its Agency Financial Report (AFR); data required are essential because State Exchange data are not otherwise available to HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM applicability date and transition timing (§155.1605)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed subpart Q would be applicable beginning January 1, 2027. For State Exchanges that participated in IPPTA, that means SEIPM measurement beginning in 2027 for PY 2026 with reporting in 2028. State Exchanges in their first year of operation must participate in a 1-year SEIPM preparation phase prior to being required to satisfy SEIPM requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: January 1, 2027 is intended to provide sufficient time for system changes, staff training, testing, and incorporation of IPPTA lessons; technical adjustments may be made via sub-regulatory guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key SEIPM definitions (§155.1610)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codified definitions for terms critical to SEIPM including Annual Program Schedule; Administrative Appeal; Administrative Appeal Decision; Corrective Action Plan (CAP); Difference Resolution; Difference Resolution Decision; Error; Measurement Year; Reporting Year; Sampled Unit Assessment Package; State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM); SEIPM Cycle; Tax household.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions specify the scope and mechanics of SEIPM processes (e.g., Error = finding that State Exchange did not correctly apply specified subparts related to eligibility/enrollment/APTC calculations). These definitions structure timelines (plan year/Measurement Year/Reporting Year) and review/appeal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information submission framework (three parts) (§155.1615)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual information submission from each State Exchange would consist of: (1) program documentation (policy/operational/technical documentation and data architecture), (2) the universe (summary listing of tax households that received APTC for the plan year from which HHS will draw a random sample), and (3) tax household data (detailed data for each sampled tax household necessary to determine proper/improper payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS would issue an Annual Program Schedule to specify due dates (proposed no later than January 5 of the Measurement Year). Program documentation enables development of State-specific review criteria; data are required for statistically valid sampling and weighted monetary estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program documentation requirements (§155.1615(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges must submit or make available policy, operational, and technical documentation concerning business rules and APTC calculations related to enrollment and eligibility processes, and information describing data system architecture (e.g., entity relationship diagrams and data dictionaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional parameters will be provided in sub-regulatory guidance. Program documentation is essential to assess alignment with Federal requirements and to develop State-specific review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universe data elements required (§155.1615(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each tax household in the universe, State Exchanges must submit or make available: (1) Exchange assigned policy identifier; (2) tax household grouping identifier; (3) SSN inconsistency indicator; (4) citizenship inconsistency indicator; (5) lawful presence inconsistency indicator; (6) annual income inconsistency indicator; (7) non-employer sponsored MEC inconsistency indicator; (8) employer sponsored MEC inconsistency indicator; (9) incarceration inconsistency indicator; (10) residency inconsistency indicator; (11) number of tax household members; and (12) APTC amount paid over the plan year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistency indicators identify presence/number of data match inconsistencies and support risk-based stratification. Total APTC amounts are needed to calculate monetary weights for improper payment estimates. A comprehensive universe is necessary for representative sampling and valid sampling weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax household sample data elements (§155.1615(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each sampled tax household, State Exchanges must submit detailed information including: APTC calculation inputs (monthly enrollee premium amounts, monthly APTC amounts, monthly SLCSP amounts, EHB-attributable premium portions); enrollment information (effectuation dates, premium payment amounts, policy start/end dates); SEP determination information (consumer attestations, documentary evidence, electronic verification info); QHP certification/timing/coverage area/decertification info; person-level attestations/demographics; APTC eligibility determinations and records of verifications including electronic sources and timing; manual verification documentation and adjudication timing; redetermination processes and results; and consumer-submitted documents used to establish eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are drawn from the FFE improper payment measurement experience and IPPTA lessons; they enable HHS to reconstruct eligibility determinations and validate APTC calculations and root causes of improper payments. HHS seeks comment on additional elements or operational challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow flexible data submission formats and use of Data Request Form (DRF)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEIPM would use the DRF (developed during IPPTA) for data collection while allowing flexibility where State Exchange data architectures conflict with DRF structure—permitting native formats in such instances and accepting manual submissions when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS automated the DRF data validation and will coordinate with State Exchanges to correct inconsistencies. Flexibility is intended to lessen burden while preserving the data needed for measurement. HHS solicits comments on alternative submission mechanisms, file formats, and technical specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Program Schedule timing (§155.1615(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would issue an Annual Program Schedule to each State Exchange no later than January 5 of the Measurement Year specifying dates for all information due to HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timeline is intended to give State Exchanges clear guidance and sufficient advance notice to plan and allocate resources for compliance in each Measurement Year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling methodology and objectives (§155.1620(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each calendar year, HHS would calculate sample sizes aggregated across all State Exchanges designed to (a) produce a highly precise aggregate estimate for all State Exchanges and (b) generate individual State Exchange estimates that meet minimum statistical validity thresholds for program management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology balances national-level precision (primary statutory requirement) with State-level management needs; recognizes that perfect state-level precision is infeasible without very large samples; aggregate estimates are weighted by State Exchange APTC size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for determining State-specific sample sizes (§155.1620(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State-specific sample sizes would consider: (i) overall APTC expenditures associated with the State Exchange (larger expenditures generally warrant larger samples); (ii) State-level precision goals for the SEIPM cycle (may vary by State based on size and impact); and (iii) the State Exchange's prior improper payment rate and variability (higher or more variable rates may require larger samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors ensure allocation of sampling effort proportional to financial risk and measurement needs and allow adjustments across cycles based on past performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum and maximum sample sizes (§155.1620(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would establish minimum and maximum sample sizes to ensure statistical validity while maintaining operational feasibility across Exchanges of varying sizes; smaller Exchanges may have wider confidence intervals but must meet minimum validity thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimums ensure every State Exchange's estimate is meaningful for oversight; maximums constrain burden and cost. The primary focus remains producing a precise national estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling unit and selection procedures (§155.1620(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes to use the tax household as the sampling unit and to select random samples of tax households annually from the universe data provided by each State Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax household is the appropriate unit because income and circumstances considered together determine APTC; random sampling supports representativeness for aggregate and State-level estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation, weighting, and reporting of improper payment estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would aggregate estimated dollar amounts of improper payments from each State Exchange to produce a national estimated amount of improper payments, weighting estimates by State Exchange size (total APTC) so larger APTC States have more influence on the aggregate rate. Estimates would be reported in the HHS AFR in accordance with OMB Circular No. A-123.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting ensures aggregate estimates reflect relative financial impact. Reporting in AFR subjects estimates to standard transparency and accountability practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) and oversight for significant improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges found to have significant improper payments could be required to develop CAPs to correct root causes; HHS would monitor CAPs until findings are resolved (consistent with §155.1200(c)(2) audit follow-up practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAPs are a mechanism to remediate material weaknesses or significant deficiencies identified by SEIPM and related audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Resolution and Administrative Appeal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: SEIPM would include a Difference Resolution process (first level) and an Administrative Appeal (second and final level) allowing State Exchanges to request HHS reconsideration of error or improper payment findings documented in a Sampled Unit Assessment Package; HHS would issue Difference Resolution Decisions and final Administrative Appeal Decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These processes provide formal opportunity for States to contest findings and for HHS to finalize determinations; appeals are limited to errors/improper payment findings documented in the Sampled Unit Assessment Package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize duplication between SEIPM and existing programmatic audits
rubrics_metrics.description: SEIPM and proposed §155.1200(e) are intended to reduce duplication between the SEIPM requirements and annual independent external programmatic audits described at §155.1200(c) and (d), by permitting SEIPM to satisfy certain audit requirements limited to subparts D and E while continuing audits for other subparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to reduce burden on State Exchanges while maintaining programmatic audit coverage for requirements not reviewed via SEIPM. Specifics would be provided in guidance and cross-references in §155.1200(d)/(e).
